official.deadline_note: Siviløkonom students in their 3rd year follow a different route: they apply in the spring of their 3rd year by emailing their CV and scholarship application letter to info@bi.no with the subject line 'BI Presidential Scholarship Application'.
official.application_cycle: Candidates admitted to a master's programme commencing Autumn 2027; all scholarships awarded by the end of April
official.status_note: The published page cycle covers candidates admitted to a master's programme commencing Autumn 2026, with every applicant informed of the decision by the end of April 2026. The next cycle repeats the same 1 March deadline.
official.tuition_coverage_note: Norwegian and international applicants who are residents of Norway, and Sivøk applicants: 'Scholarships will cover full tuition fees for each semester, for up to two years, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.' International applicants: 'Scholarships will cover full tuition fees for up to two years and a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester, if the student achieves the academic progression requirements.'
benefits: Full tuition fees for up to two years
International applicants: a stipend for living expenses of NOK 50,000 per semester
Recognition as a BI Ambassador, acting as a spokesperson, assisting in recruitment efforts and promoting a good study environment
International applicants are also considered for the Master's International Scholarship, with no separate scholarship application letter required
eligibility: A minimum overall GPA of 'A' on the ECTS scale, or the equivalent top-level grade on international grade scales

Candidates with Norwegian or international citizenship; candidates with international citizenship who have completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are considered residents of Norway for this scholarship
Admitted to the first year of a master's degree programme at campus Oslo or campus Bergen, except for the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing
Only candidates seeking their first master's degree are considered for master's scholarships
Students in the 3rd year of the Sivøk programme are eligible to apply
requirements: Always apply for the scholarship at the same time as you apply for admission on the online application portal, and upload it to the section marked 'Scholarship'
Upload a CV/resume and a scholarship application letter of maximum one page outlining why you should be considered, combined into one PDF file
A complete application for admission must be submitted and the offer of admission accepted for the scholarship application to be considered
Full study progression of 30 ECTS in each semester and a minimum cumulative GPA of 'B' on the BI ECTS scale after each academic semester
Only one scholarship is awarded per applicant, even if you apply for more than one
documents: Scholarship application letter of maximum one page, combined with the CV into a single PDF
All documentation required to be evaluated for admission to a master's programme
selection_criteria: Scholarships are awarded based on academic merit, not on financial need
All candidates are assessed according to the ECTS scale, and applicants with international bachelor's degrees have their grades converted to the ECTS scale
Other factors that may influence awarding include other academic achievements, GMAT/GRE/CAT scores, extracurricular achievements and special personal achievements
BI ensures the distribution of scholarships across master's programmes and reserves the right to prioritise specific programmes, diversity and gender distribution, or selected partner schools
coverage: Full tuition fees for up to two years
International applicants: living-expense stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester
No travel, housing or insurance coverage is stated
application_method: Applications for scholarship are not accepted by email, with the exception of 3rd-year Sivøk applicants; apply at the same time as admission on the online application portal and upload to the section marked 'Scholarship'
official.application_route: Submit the master's admission application on BI's online portal with the combined CV and one-page letter attached in the 'Scholarship' section before 1 March.
official.citizenship_residency: Norwegian or international citizenship; international citizens who completed a bachelor's degree in Norway are treated as residents of Norway for scholarship purposes
official.international_eligibility: International applicants are eligible and receive full tuition plus a NOK 50,000 per semester living-expense stipend
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Open to master's degree programmes at campus Oslo or campus Bergen, except the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing
official.description: The BI Presidential Scholarship covers full tuition fees for up to two years for admitted master's students at BI's Oslo or Bergen campuses, and adds a living-expense stipend of NOK 50,000 per semester for international applicants, provided the academic progression requirements are met. Selection is based on academic excellence rather than financial need, and recipients serve as BI Ambassadors.
official.program_type: Merit-based master's scholarship (full tuition, plus a living-expense stipend for international applicants)

not_confirmed: publication date of the next cycle page
verification.notes: The applicant-type split of the award, the ECTS 'A' threshold, the NOK 50,000 per semester stipend figure, progression requirements and the end-of-April notification timing were all read directly from BI's own scholarship page.

applicant_utility.summary: The detail that changes the value of this award is the applicant split: Norwegian and Norway-resident candidates receive tuition only, while international applicants receive tuition plus NOK 50,000 per semester, so the same application is worth materially more depending on your citizenship and where you completed your bachelor's. Your entire scholarship file is one PDF containing a CV and a one-page letter, and it must be attached inside the admission application rather than emailed. Accept the admission offer as soon as it arrives, because the scholarship is only considered once you have.
applicant_utility.best_fit: International applicants with an 'A'-level ECTS record entering an Oslo or Bergen master's who can still cover Norwegian living costs beyond the stipend.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your GPA reads as 'A' on the ECTS scale after BI's conversion, not merely on your home scale
Check the BI-Luiss Joint Masters in Marketing exclusion before settling on a programme
Merge the CV and the one-page letter into a single PDF and upload it in the 'Scholarship' section of the same application
Accept the admission offer immediately rather than waiting for the scholarship verdict
Plan from semester one around the 30 ECTS progression rule and the cumulative 'B' GPA floor
common_rejection_risks: Emailing the scholarship materials, which BI does not accept
Waiting for the scholarship decision before accepting the admission offer and losing eligibility
Dropping below 30 ECTS in a semester or under a cumulative 'B', which forfeits the award
Applying as an international citizen who actually completed a Norwegian bachelor's degree, since BI reclassifies you as domestic and the stipend disappears
Holding a previous master's degree, which removes you from consideration entirely
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Housing, flights, insurance and most daily living costs. The stipend is NOK 50,000 per semester and applies only to international applicants, while Norway-resident candidates receive tuition coverage alone.
document_audit: The letter is capped at one page and must be merged with the CV into a single PDF, so an over-long letter is a genuine failure mode
Nothing can be added after submission, so a missing admission document quietly voids the scholarship file
3rd-year Sivøk applicants use an email route to info@bi.no instead of the portal, so do not assume the portal route applies
alerts: You may apply for more than one BI scholarship, but BI awards only one per applicant
Scholarship offers are not sent with offers of admission and may arrive at any point in the admission cycle
Offers not accepted by the date indicated are withdrawn and awarded to another candidate
All scholarships are awarded by the end of April except the A. Wilhelmsen Foundation Scholarship and the BI-Luiss Joint Master in Marketing Scholarship, which come later in the spring
Decisions are final, non-negotiable and cannot be appealed
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: A single portal submission combining admission and scholarship, with every applicant informed of the decision by the end of April and the offer accepted inside a stated window.
